reason: The provided sources contain robust, multi-sourced facts detailing Voyager 2's historic 1989 Neptune encounter and its unexpected atmospheric discoveries.
story: In August 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 completed its Grand Tour by making humanity's first and only flyby of Neptune. Swooping just 3,000 miles above the ice giant's north pole, the probe revealed a vivid blue world colored by atmospheric methane. Expecting a frozen, quiet planet, scientists were shocked to find intense atmospheric activity. Voyager 2 recorded wind speeds topping 1,000 miles per hour—the fastest ever measured anywhere in the solar system—alongside a massive Earth-sized storm called the Great Dark Spot. The probe also discovered six new moons and four rings surrounding Neptune. Continuing on to Neptune's largest moon, Triton, Voyager 2 photographed active ice volcanoes spewing material skyward despite surface temperatures dropping to minus 391 degrees Fahrenheit. At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, scientists celebrated the final planetary encounter of the Voyager mission with a live performance by rock legend Chuck Berry.
angle: At the freezing outer edge of the solar system, Neptune registered the fastest wind speeds ever recorded anywhere in the solar system, exceeding 1,000 miles per hour.

claims.claim: Voyager 2 completed its closest flyby of Neptune on August 25, 1989.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to ever visit Neptune.
Neptune's blue color is caused by the presence of methane in its atmosphere.
Voyager 2 recorded winds on Neptune topping 1,000 miles per hour.
The winds measured on Neptune were the fastest recorded anywhere in the solar system.
Voyager 2 discovered a giant Earth-sized storm on Neptune dubbed the Great Dark Spot.
Voyager 2 discovered six previously unknown moons orbiting Neptune.
Voyager 2 confirmed the existence of four rings around Neptune.
Voyager 2 swooped approximately 3,000 miles (4,950 kilometers) above Neptune's north pole.
Voyager 2 discovered active geysers or ice volcanoes erupting on Triton.
Triton had a recorded surface temperature of minus 391 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 235 degrees Celsius).
The Neptune flyby was the final planetary encounter of Voyager 2's Grand Tour.
Rock musician Chuck Berry performed live at JPL to celebrate the Neptune encounter.
Ed Stone served as project scientist for the Voyager mission.
Voyager 2 was launched by NASA in August 1977.
